clue.text: Simple things one caught, fish coming round

indicators.note: the fish word comes round, enclosing the other two pieces

parts.note: the bass is a fish
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler lists the basics: one fish caught, and another swimming round.
explanation.definitionFit: Basics are fundamentals, the elementary matters anyone must learn first.

clue.text: Times in which to get cross, sullen

indicators.note: in which to get means the cross word goes inside the times word

parts.note: by, as in three by four, means times
a rood is a cross, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: Moody periods when one becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the noun, a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooding and moody, sunk in sullen thought.

clue.text: Liaises to reorganise area now in Poland

indicators.note: to reorganise asks us to rearrange the letters of the first word

explanation.surface: Coordinators restructure a region of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region, most of it today part of Poland.

clue.text: Cold little boy is sweet

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Andy is a short form of Andrew, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small child, cold, is still lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is an American word for a confection or a boiled sweet.

clue.text: Made a jump seconds before crash

indicators.note: before puts the seconds letter ahead of the crash word

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor crash, especially of a car

explanation.surface: Someone leapt clear a moment before a car collision.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is everyday British slang for a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of spring, which means to leap.

clue.text: Frenchman demonstrated and shouted, getting led off

parts.note: proven means demonstrated to be true

indicators.note: off says the letters of the word before it are removed

parts.note: called means shouted out

explanation.surface: A Frenchman proved his point, yelling as he was led away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LED from CALLED to leave CAL; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Provencal is a native of Provence in southern France.

clue.text: Opposing what in France is seen as old-fashioned

parts.note: anti means against or opposing
que is French for what

explanation.surface: Disapproving of what the French regard as outmoded.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique describes something old, from an earlier era.

clue.text: Extra piece from good American group

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A bonus item from a fine American band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra piece' suggests a bonus; it is sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusset is a triangular piece of fabric inserted to strengthen or enlarge a garment.

clue.text: Pickle from Caribbean island in short supply

indicators.note: in short supply says the island's name is cut down, kept only in part

parts.note: Jamaica is an island in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A relish imported from the West Indies is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a relish; it is a predicament. Shortening JAMAICA to its first three letters leaves the answer, also its standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for an awkward predicament or tight spot.

clue.text: Infant Shaw curiously involved in something trivial as a writer

indicators.note: involved in means the scrambled letters sit inside the trivial word

parts.note: a jot is a tiny trivial amount

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of Infant Shaw are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: A baby playwright oddly caught up in trifles as an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw, a famous playwright, tempts you to look for him; he is only fodder, and the definition is the last word. 'curiously' scrambles the letters, and 'involved in' sets them inside the trivial word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Badly run trains, dilemma needing to be sorted out

indicators.note: needing to be sorted out says the letters of trains and dilemma must be put into order

explanation.surface: A rail service mismanaged, a problem requiring fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To maladminister is to manage public affairs incompetently.

clue.text: Soldiers come down on old American city

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
an aircraft that comes down lands

explanation.surface: Troops parachute onto an old city in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in Florida, in the United States.

clue.text: Rodents bringing a disease to island

parts.note: gout is a disease causing painful joints

explanation.surface: Rats carrying an illness onto an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are burrowing rodents of Central and South America.

clue.text: Lifeless soprano participating in service

indicators.note: participating in means the soprano letter goes inside the service word

parts.note: duty is service done for others

explanation.surface: A dreary soprano is singing at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifeless' suggests dead; here it means dull and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty can mean dry and dull, like something long neglected.

clue.text: Be a square, slamming ornamental design

indicators.note: slamming, in the sense of knocking about, tells us to batter these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Stop being old-fashioned and scorn this decorative pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slamming' looks like criticising, but it is the anagram signal for BE A SQUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a decorative style of intertwined lines and foliage.

clue.text: Tease ridiculous-looking team with cheeky kit

indicators.note: ridiculous-looking says the following words are made into a silly new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mocking a sports side for wearing absurd, cheeky strips.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TEAM, CHEEKY and KIT; 'with' just links them. The phrase is British slang for mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to mock or make fun of someone, the phrase being British slang.

clue.text: Get money from Irishman turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue tells us to read the Irishman's name upwards

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Asking an Irishman who arrives for some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap someone is to ask them for a loan or gift of cash.

clue.text: Gosh, I meet crazy boat race crew maybe!

indicators.note: crazy tells us the letters of the preceding words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the mad meeting of rowing crews.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew is an eight, a group of eight people; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight people, like a rowing crew, is an eightsome.

clue.text: Something dried up? That's disgusting!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: hay is grass that has been dried

explanation.surface: A dried-up something prompts a cry of revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah is an exclamation expressing disgust or derision.

clue.text: Impure language that sounds as if it's for the birds

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like something else

parts.note: a language for the birds would be pigeon English

explanation.surface: A mixed tongue that seems fit only for birds to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the birds' is also slang for worthless, which supports the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin is a simplified mixed language used between peoples with no common tongue.

clue.text: Home terrific we hear? This person won't say thank you

definitions.text: This person won't say thank you

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: we hear says a word that sounds like terrific is wanted

parts.note: great means terrific

explanation.surface: Someone says home is wonderful but gives no thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person.

clue.text: Son possessing and using bathroom items?

parts.note: having means possessing

explanation.surface: A boy owns and uses toiletries.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, hence the question mark: shaving needs razor and foam.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing whiskers with a razor and foam, kept by the washbasin.

clue.text: Attacks despicable person leading English society

parts.note: a snip is an insignificant or impudent person, used dismissively

explanation.surface: A villain at the head of high English society mounts assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' places the person ahead of the other two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipes are sniping criticisms, sly verbal attacks.

clue.text: Bit of food a Greek character fed to the dog?

indicators.note: fed to means the pieces go inside the dog word

parts.note: a dog is a typical pet
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Feeding a morsel to the family dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a small nut eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Are they wise when others have succumbed to darkness?

definitions.text: Are they wise when others have succumbed to darkness?

parts.words: Are they wise when others have succumbed to darkness?
parts.note: wise birds associated with darkness are owls; people who stay awake late while others sleep share their name

explanation.surface: Asking whether those still awake at night are clever.
explanation.definitionFit: People who stay up late are named after the nocturnal bird thought wise.

clue.text: Disturb fish by double bend

parts.note: an S shape is a double bend
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Upset a fish by bending it twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link, putting the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake someone is to unsettle or upset them.

clue.text: Capital person with inner energy

indicators.note: with inner means the energy letter goes inside the person word

parts.note: soul means person, as in not a soul
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A spirited person full of vitality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

clue.text: No possibility of drama? There might be in this decisive game

definitions.meaning: if a play is off, the theatre performance is cancelled
an extra match to settle a tie

explanation.surface: A tie-breaking match may cancel all theatrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Play off read literally is cancelled drama; as one word it is a tie-break match.

clue.text: One may have special tie on - - a nob, ob standing out?

indicators.note: special here means altered, so the letters are rearranged
standing out means those two letters leave the phrase a nob

explanation.surface: A posh old boy in his school tie, a nob through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove OB from A NOB to get AN, add TIE ON, and rearrange those letters. Old Etonians are often wealthy, wearing their school tie.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is one who went to Eton, the elite English boarding school.

clue.text: Sailor seen as the reverse of someone contemptible

indicators.note: the reverse of tells us to read the contemptible word backwards

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A seaman is the opposite of a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is an old informal word for a seaman.

clue.text: Notice signal to stop and get get angry

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
a red light is the signal to stop

explanation.surface: Spot a red light and lose your temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held prints 'get' twice; the first is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom meaning to become furious.

clue.text: Female idle? Lift may be preferred to this!

definitions.text: Lift may be preferred to this!

parts.note: idle talk is light, trivial talk

explanation.surface: A lazy woman takes the elevator rather than climbing stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' means elevator, the British word: many prefer it to a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of stairs between floors, which an elevator spares you.
